previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for fevers following a recent AV fistula revision. She developed postoperative fatigue, vomiting, and fever, prompting evaluation. Initial labs showed elevated inflammatory markers and transaminitis. Blood cultures were negative to date, and she remained afebrile after 24 hours without antibiotics. Her symptoms were attributed to likely transient bacteremia or viral illness. She also reported worsening exertional shortness of breath; chest imaging showed no acute process, and a stress test was ordered. Abdominal ultrasound revealed 1 cm common bile duct dilation, previously noted intermittently, with plans for outpatient MRCP. She improved clinically, returned to baseline, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in primary care, cardiology, and gastroenterology.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior studies with the latest non-contrast CT head on
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast multiplanar, multisequence T1- and T2-weighted images
were acquired through the head.  Diffusion-weighted images and ADC maps were
also obtained for evaluation.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute infarct or hemorrhage.  The ventricles and sulci
are normal in size for age and symmetric in configuration.  There is no shift
of normally midline structures.  The gray-white matter differentiation is
preserved.  Major vascular flow voids are present.  

There are mild-to-moderate confluence periventricular and scattered
subcortical white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, nonspecific, but likely
representing sequelae of chronic microvascular ischemic disease.  In the left
anterior temporal lobe, there is a small focal FLAIR signal abnormality
possibly extending to the cortex (image ___ and ___, could represent an
old small infarct or small vessel ischemia.

The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids air cells are clear.  The globes
are symmetric and unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial abnormality.  Specifically, no acute infarct or
hemorrhage.

2.  Chronic microvascular ischemic disease.  A small FLAIR-hyperintense focus
in the left anterior temporal lobe could relate to this, or represent an old
discrete infarct.

COMMENT: An additional T2-/FLAIR-hyperintense focus in the superficial left
superior frontal gyrus (4,6:20) is probably unchanged since ___ and likely
represents an old subcortical infarct.

HISTORY:  ___ year old woman with lupus, ESRD, intermittent fevers &
cholestasis. Please evaluate for abnormalities of biliary tree

COMPARISON:  ___ 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 T
magnet, without intravenous contrast administration.  1 mL of Gadavist was
ingested orally.  It should be noted that the patient was unable to complete
the 3D MRCP portion of the exam. 

FINDINGS:

LUNG BASES:  There is atelectasis at the left lung base.  

ABDOMEN:  The liver and spleen are low in T1 and T2 signal intensity and
demonstrate an increase in signal intensity on in-phase (latery echo) T1
weighted imaging, compatible with secondary hemosiderosis.  There is a T2
hyperintensity within the spleen which is incompletely imaged and may
represent either a cyst or hemangioma.  

The common bile duct is dilated measuring up to 1 cm, without evidence of a
obstructive lesion in the ampulla. The common bile duct tapers as it enters
into the ampullary region. The pancreas is normal in signal intensity.  Note
is made of a pancreas divisum.  

The adrenal glands are normal.  Bilaterally the kidneys are small and
demonstrate multiple cystic lesions.  One small cyst within the upper pole of
the left kidney demonstrates hyperintense T1 signal compatible with hemorrhage
(62:8).  

The visualized small and large bowel appear unremarkable.  There is no
ascites. The aorta is of normal caliber.  Prominent periaortic lymph nodes are
appreciated, nonspecific for instance, left periaortic node measuring up to 12
mm (13:4). 

BONE MARROW:   Diffusely low signal intensity on T2 weighted images bone
marrow is appreciated, as well as hyperintense signal intensity at the
endplates.  This may be related to changes of metabolic bone disease.  

IMPRESSION:

1. The common bile duct is dilated but tapers as it enters the ampulla.  This
may reflect a component of sphincter of Oddi dysfunction or ampullary
stenosis.  There is no obstructing mass lesion. 

2. Findings are compatible with secondary hemosiderosis within the the liver
and spleen. 

3. Small kidneys reflect medical renal disease with multiple cysts.  

4. Pancreas divisum.
